quarterly_data.signal: Q2 adjusted revenue was $919 million (GAAP $889 million; the $30 million difference is tariff refunds passed through to customers in the second half), exceeding the top end of guidance and rising 9.5% sequentially and 21% year over year. Growth was driven by an 18% year-over-year volume increase plus a 2% increase in average selling prices, with 1% of favourable FX. Adjusted gross margin was 22.6% and adjusted operating margin 5.8%, up sharply from 2.6% in Q1 and 1.4% in Q2 2025. EBITDA was $105 million for an 11.4% adjusted EBITDA margin, up from 9.3% in Q1, and EPS was $0.19 versus $0.05 in Q1 and a $0.07 adjusted loss a year ago. Growth came across all product technologies, end markets, channels and regions.
quarterly_data.figure: Q2 adjusted revenue $919M (+9.5% QoQ, +21% YoY); adjusted gross margin 22.6%; adjusted operating margin 5.8%; EPS $0.19

quarterly_data.signal: Q3 2026 guidance: revenue of $945-975 million, a 21.4% year-over-year and 4.5% sequential increase at the midpoint after allowing for European seasonality. Gross margin is guided to 24.0% plus or minus 50 basis points - reaching the 24% target ONE QUARTER SOONER than the previous goal of exiting the year at that level. SG&A is guided to $155 million plus or minus $3 million, depreciation approximately $54 million ($215 million for the full year), interest expense approximately $7 million and the effective tax rate 35-40%. Management reaffirmed the strategic-plan gross margin target of 30% and said the 2028 timeline for it is not being pulled into early 2027.
quarterly_data.figure: Q3 guide $945M-$975M (+21.4% YoY); gross margin 24.0% ±50bps, one quarter ahead of plan; 30% GM strategic target intact

quarterly_data.signal: Order book at multi-decade highs: Q2 book-to-bill was 1.32, with semiconductors at 1.23 and passives at 1.40, and Q2 was a record high for resistor and inductor bookings. Total backlog grew 18% to $1.9 BILLION, equal to 6.1 months. In the Americas, book-to-bill was 1.5 and orders for passives reached the highest level seen in MORE THAN 20 YEARS. Customers are extending visibility to secure supply - many forecasting six months out to replenish their own inventories, and AI-driven demand has led numerous customers to place orders BEYOND 52 WEEKS to hold a place in Vishay's production loading. Some automotive customers are providing 12-to-18-month forecasts.
quarterly_data.figure: Book-to-bill 1.32 (semis 1.23, passives 1.40); backlog +18% to $1.9B (6.1 months); Americas book-to-bill 1.5; AI customers ordering beyond 52 weeks

quarterly_data.signal: Component supply is tightening and pricing is rising. Industry lead times are stretching and customers are concerned about availability and assurance of supply. Vishay began announcing price increases in Q4 2025 tied to rising metals, materials and logistics costs and continued through Q1 and Q2; ABOUT ONE THIRD of running part numbers now have announced price increases, some of which landed in Q2 results. CEO Joel Smejkal said the increases are real rather than 'paper' and that Vishay reprices the backlog quickly so customers cannot pull orders ahead of them. On whether this is double ordering: management says it is still fairly rational - point-of-sale consumption is growing, distribution inventory FELL to 18 weeks from 20 weeks, and distributors have been unable to replenish despite wanting to. Customers are also increasingly requesting WESTERN supply of electronic components, which suits Vishay's footprint. Management describes the industry as early in the upcycle.
quarterly_data.figure: ~1/3 of running part numbers have announced price increases; distribution inventory down to 18 weeks from 20

quarterly_data.signal: AI is now a named demand driver across the portfolio. Industrial revenue rose 16.2% sequentially and 30.1% year over year on smart grid, AI POWER and high-voltage DC projects plus factory automation, with bookings up for industrial power applications serving power conversion and tooling projects for AI data centers as EMS customers accelerate AI investment. Vishay is increasing its part count on new projects as customers add its passives to AI POWER MANAGEMENT solutions. The 'other' end market (telecom, computing, consumer) grew 11.3% sequentially and 28.4% year over year on AI-related programs in Asia and higher demand for AI OPTICAL COMMUNICATION NETWORK SWITCHES. Management notes Vishay can populate more than 80% of the components on a board in a power application, and that competitors' inability to supply is generating escalation opportunities. Non-AI customers are now also escalating to secure manufacturing slots.
quarterly_data.figure: Industrial +16.2% QoQ / +30.1% YoY; other (telecom/computing/consumer) +11.3% QoQ / +28.4% YoY

quarterly_data.signal: Capacity build-out, funded by $900 million invested during the trough years plus a new equity raise. Full-year 2026 capex is $400-440 million with about half earmarked for the 12-inch fab in Germany (Itzehoe): all equipment is assembled, installation completes in Q3, engineering wafers start toward the end of the year and NON-AUTOMOTIVE PRODUCTION REMAINS ON TRACK FOR MID-2027. At the Newport fab, nine of ten automotive customer audits are complete with PCN program approvals expected monthly through year end, which will raise Newport utilisation and free capacity at the Itzehoe 8-inch fab. Vishay is also ramping production at two foundries in KOREA plus another in CHINA from Q3, explicitly to add wafer capacity for AI MOSFETs and diodes in the later part of the year, and is working to add dedicated in-house back-end capacity to cut dependence on outside subcontractors. Q2 capex was $95 million including approximately $66 million for the German fab.
quarterly_data.figure: FY2026 capex $400M-$440M (~half for the 12-inch German fab); Q2 capex $95M incl. ~$66M for Germany; 2 Korean foundries + 1 China foundry ramping in Q3; German fab non-auto production mid-2027

quarterly_data.signal: On the MLCC versus polymer tantalum debate for AI power: Vishay's MLCCs are specialised products aimed at military and medical, though it picks up AI and compute orders when other MLCC suppliers' lead times run long. Management says polymer tantalum demand is still GROWING in both automotive and AI, with very long competitor lead times and strong customer interest in adding Vishay as a source. Polymer capacitor output is being expanded at existing locations by the end of the year plus a capacity expansion at a new site in La Laguna, Mexico, and automotive qualifications continue at La Laguna and Juarez. Design wins in the quarter covered industrial power management, smart grid battery backup, energy storage systems, power modules for industrial heating, solar inverters and ADAS. Vishay continues to execute a silicon carbide strategy and GaN development for the wide bandgap market.

Other end markets and channel: aerospace and defense revenue rose 4.2% sequentially and 15.4% year over year on funded U.S. defense programs including accelerated component replenishment for multiple missile programs, with distribution bookings up sharply ahead of Department of Defense funding for next-generation radar, high-energy weapons for drone defense, Golden Dome and LEO constellations. Automotive rose 3.6% sequentially and 10.1% year over year on rising electronic content for driver assist, autonomous driving and hybrid/EV adoption. Healthcare rose 7% sequentially and 14.7% year over year. Distribution grew to 58% of revenue from 55%, up 15.6% sequentially and 24.2% year over year, with point-of-sale up 4.7% sequentially and 20.5% year over year. Asia accounted for over half the sequential revenue increase, up 12.5%; the Americas grew 14.1%.
quarterly_data.figure: A&D +4.2% QoQ / +15.4% YoY; automotive +3.6% / +10.1%; healthcare +7% / +14.7%; distribution 58% of revenue, POS +20.5% YoY

quarterly_data.signal: Balance sheet and cash: Vishay completed a public offering of 17.25 million shares, receiving $830 million net of issuance costs, explicitly to accelerate growth initiatives and invest across semiconductors and passives IN PARALLEL rather than sequentially, and to reignite a disciplined M&A process. Q2 operating cash flow was $105 million and free cash flow $10 million (versus negative $47 million in Q1); full-year 2026 free cash flow is still expected to be NEGATIVE because of capacity expansion. Cash and short-term investments ended at $1.3 billion with $238 million outstanding on the revolver, repaid in July; accessible revolver capacity rose from $423 million to approximately $661 million after repayment. The quarterly dividend was $13.6 million and no shares were repurchased. The cash conversion cycle improved to 110 days from 116, with inventory up slightly to $807 million on safety stock and backlog support.
quarterly_data.figure: $830M net equity raise; $1.3B cash and short-term investments; Q2 OCF $105M, FCF $10M; FY2026 FCF expected negative
